title: D Minor Open-Chord with Little-Finger Variant (Beginner Guitar)
summary: This beginner-friendly tutorial teaches a D minor open-chord with an alternative fingering that uses the little finger on the third fret of the B string. The instructor contrasts this approach with the traditional 1-2-3 fingering, explaining why the little finger can be easier to position and how it helps the hand adapt to pressing strings. The video provides exact finger placements—index on the 1st fret of the high E string, middle on the 2nd fret of the G string, and the pinky on the 3rd fret of the B string—while emphasizing the standard practice of starting with an open D string (the 4th). It also covers common problems (muted 4th string, buzzing from the little finger), troubleshooting tips (using the 3rd finger if buzzing persists), and a relaxation-based drill to find a comfortable hand/arm position before strumming and checking the chord.
topics: First finger on 1st fret of high E string
Second finger on 2nd fret of G string
Little finger on 3rd fret of B string
Do not play the thickest two strings
String order: 4th string open, 3rd fret G string, 2nd fret B string, 1st fret high E string
Sound of the D minor chord
Muting issues caused by finger position
Little finger tip placement and pressure
Buzzing issues and alternative fingering (3rd finger)
Hand/arm relaxation technique (shoulders down, elbow movement)
Finding a comfortable chord position through practice
Posture and positional checks (lifting fingers, strumming to test)

It contrasts this with the traditional 1-2-3 fingering, explains why the little finger approach can be easier for beginners, and details common issues such as muting the open 4th string and buzzing from the little finger. It also covers hand/posture tips to help players find a comfortable position and prepares for a practice drill that confirms correct fingering by strumming after making adjustments.

featured_techniques.technique: D minor open-chord fingering variant: index finger on 1st fret of the high E string, middle finger on 2nd fret of the G string, pinky on 3rd fret of the B string, with the 4th string open.
Exact string order and fretting for the Dm variant: pluck 4th string open, then 3rd string (2nd fret), then 2nd string (3rd fret), then 1st string (1st fret).
Mute/fret correction: ensure the 2nd finger does not mute the open 4th string; adjust finger height and angle accordingly.
Little finger tip placement and pressure: keep the little finger on the fret with the tip, avoiding contact with the 3rd string, to prevent buzzing.
Relaxation drill: lift fingers and strum to check corrections; gradually relax the hand, arm, and shoulder posture to find a comfortable chord position.
